fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar currently decides and performs Jira work across the differ, generic apply wrapper, Cloud ACLI/REST, Jira DC SDK, handlers, and batch orchestration. Retry ownership is multiplied: one logical postcondition can cross nested loops, whole compound updates can replay after a late failure, provider delay can be capped and retried early, and terminal failures do not have a stable per-ticket versus batch scope. No existing mechanism models these outcomes: the reconciler's only breaker (`classify.check_blast_radius`) is a per-pass blast-radius acting-fraction guard against mass mutation, not an endpoint-failure fuse.

## Outcome
Build one provider-neutral coordinator around immutable observation and pure per-ticket `TicketPlan` values. Each plan carries existing `Mutation` values, lifecycle intents, dependencies, diagnostics, and disposition. Global selection/filter/caps run before any lifecycle or remote effect. Concrete adapters own physical replay, timeouts, cleanup, SDK retry disablement, and provider decoding; core owns commit-unknown recovery, re-observation/replanning, dependency deferral, the finite-pass fuse, and exact ticket/pass outcomes.

## Approved policy
- At most three physical invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep per logical postcondition, including one observe/replan cycle; fallback delays are approximately 2s then 4s with nonnegative jitter.
- `Retry-After` or equivalent is a lower bound. If it cannot fit, return `retry_not_before` for a later pass rather than retrying early.
- Add a new endpoint-failure scoped fuse (none exists today; the reconciler has no rolling/consecutive failure-rate breaker). An endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes across at least two tickets. Provider scope additionally requires two endpoint families. Matching success resets the scope. Attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, and opaque diagnostics do not count. The existing per-pass blast-radius acting-fraction guard (`classify.check_blast_radius`) is a distinct mass-mutation protection and is RETAINED unchanged; the fuse adds endpoint-failure protection and does not remove blast-radius protection.
- Authoritative credential, configuration, quota, rate, issue, endpoint, tenant, and global scopes retain their direct classified behavior.
- Create containment is label-first (`rebar-id:<local_id>`), optional property second, then safety-abort with the known key if local persistence fails.

## Delivery slices
1. Prove one Cloud/DC operation end to end through normalized outcomes and the single retry budget with deterministic fake transports.
2. Produce immutable shadow plans and versioned preview lifecycle intents from one observation with zero remote/local effects.
3. Cut non-create operations to the coordinator with dependency deferral, exact partial outcomes, retry deferral, and scoped fuse.
4. Cut create and lifecycle recovery to the RP-02 transaction seam with commit-unknown containment.
5. Finish expand/contract cutover, remove legacy retry/write fallbacks, and seal manifests, observability, cursor behavior, documentation, and bounded live validation.

## Compatibility / rollback
Shadow planning first compares existing mutation shape and provider-neutral outcomes without writes. Cutover is by operation family and never dual-writes. Before contract removal, an operation can return to the legacy dispatcher. Rollback never deletes a successful Jira effect; commit-unknown work is re-observed. Existing ticket/event/binding shapes remain readable, and preview adds versioned lifecycle intent fields without changing the existing mutation shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One observation deterministically produces per-ticket plans whose selection, caps, dependencies, diagnostics, dispositions, mutations, and lifecycle intents are testable without Jira or filesystem writes.
- [x] Cloud ACLI/REST and Jira DC execute each logical postcondition within one three-call/15-second budget, disable hidden SDK retry, honor provider lower bounds, and defer long waits with `retry_not_before`.
- [x] The riskiest DC capability — that the real Jira DC SDK honors `max_retries=0` by exposing `_session.max_retries == 0` — is proven in-session in S1 against the actual `jira` 3.10.5 library via an offline construction test (no network/credentials), not only via fake transports.
- [x] The coordinator classifies auto-healed, retryable, permanent, commit-unknown, ticket-local, endpoint, tenant, provider, and global outcomes with exact per-ticket and pass tallies.
- [x] The approved three-consecutive scoped fuse triggers only from normalized exhausted logical outcomes and does not stop historically successful/partially successful replay fixtures prematurely.
- [x] Create tests prove label-first containment, optional property enrichment, known-key safety-abort, and no duplicate create after timeout or persistence failure.
- [x] Shadow/cutover tests prove no dual-write, safe fallback before legacy removal, versioned preview compatibility, fail-loud unsupported production paths, and no rollback deletion of successful Jira work.
- [x] [operator-attested] A **Live External Integration** workflow runs GREEN in GitHub Actions, exercising this epic's coordinator, create/binding-lifecycle, commit-unknown recovery, and endpoint/provider fuse functionality end-to-end against BOTH a live **Jira Cloud** instance and a live **Jira Data Center** instance (real transports and credentials, not deterministic fakes). Scope differs by instance for shared-production safety, and each scope is faithful to what that instance can safely bear:
  provenance: environment=live Jira Cloud (project REB, shared prod; bounded, self-cleaning) + ephemeral live Jira Data Center (GitHub Actions external-integration.yml); principal=CI external-integration service credentials; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — run 33137402410 ran GREEN on BOTH the bounded Cloud mutation lane and the ephemeral DC harness lane end-to-end; run URL commented on this epic.
  - **Data Center** (an ephemeral, isolated instance the workflow spins up and tears down) — the FULL multi-issue reconcile suite: coordinator create/binding-lifecycle, commit-unknown recovery, and fuse across many issues and repeated convergence passes.
  - **Jira Cloud** (shared production, project REB) — the SAME coordinator create/binding-lifecycle, commit-unknown recovery, and fuse paths exercised end-to-end, but BOUNDED to uniquely-labeled throwaway issues that the lane ALWAYS deletes (a `finally`/teardown sweep keyed on the run's unique `rebar-id:` label) — NO full-project reconcile or write-back against shared prod — plus a self-cleaning bridge capability probe (create/label/property/JQL-search/delete). This is the sanctioned bounded interpretation established when a full shared-prod reconcile was found unsafe; it validates the coordinator against a real Cloud transport without endangering shared data.
  This live run is a REQUIRED gate: the epic MUST NOT be closed until both the DC lane and the bounded Cloud lane have passed GREEN.
